items.title: Captain Verne Streckfus Interview, 1960-09-22
items.q: It's an A1 piano player. He can call on right quick. In fact, we've had a five-pound number eight years. He took it off on the other boats in the afternoon. And he plays it in the afternoon.

ctx.x: He was on the boat. He was on the boat. He was on the boat. He was on the boat. What about Steve Lewis? When was he on the boat? I don't remember Steve Lewis. He was supposed to play the Kalanke here. I think in his... Put a raincoat on or something. Walk out of that water. Maybe they all did. Well, they could. But they always put cotton in the rear. They did that. Because it was pretty loud. You see, if you could play it louder. Except for the one of the steam pressure, they have a rain.

They'd foul them. If you wanted to carry a great distance and made it hard for the panel player to play it. So you only have 28 keys. And you know, they're not going to play the Clack. But they always put cotton in the rear. They did that. Because it was pretty loud. You see, if you could play it louder. Except for the one of the steam pressure, they have a rain. They foul them. No, I wish I had known about it.
